Line 315: `log "verification passed ✓"` — no enclosing condition. Lines 383-385: `if [ "${FAIL:-0}" -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi` — FAIL is preserved here, script exits 1 correctly. The "verification passed" line fires unconditionally between the two.
findings.impact: Any operator who reads the terminal output on a failed verification sees contradictory messages. More critically, if stdout is captured for a CI dry-run audit log the log will contain "verification passed ✓" even when branch protection is in a partial post-PUT/pre-POST state. The log block that follows also gets emitted with the partial after-state, so the audit trail does not clearly record failure. The attending operator's only reliable signal is the non-zero exit code.
findings.mitigation: Wrap lines 315-318 in `if [ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]; then ... fi`. The fall-through path for FAIL≠0 should NOT reach the passed message; it should jump directly to the log-block emission. Alternatively add `else log "verification FAILED — see error(s) above"` inside the existing FAIL block and guard line 315 accordingly.

findings.claim: The `--repo` path-traversal guard regex `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` accepts `owner/..` as a valid repo name because `..` satisfies `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` (the dot character is explicitly included in the class and `+` requires only one character minimum). The guard was added to prevent path traversal in URL construction; `..` is the canonical path-traversal primitive.
findings.evidence: enable-required-check.sh line 193: `if ! printf '%s' "$REPO" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$'; then`. Character class `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` includes literal dot `.`. The string `..` matches as two dot characters. Downstream at line 283: `gh api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/branches/${BRANCH}/protection"` — a repo value of `owner/..` produces the path `repos/owner/../branches/...`; whether gh URL-normalises this before sending is implementation-dependent. The same class also permits repo names starting with a dot (e.g., `.hidden`), which GitHub does not allow.
findings.impact: If gh passes the path raw to the HTTP stack, `repos/owner/../branches/main/protection` traverses to `repos/owner` then descends into `branches/main/protection`, which is a distinct API endpoint. In practice GitHub's API server would likely return 404 or 400, not silently act on a wrong endpoint, so exploitation risk is low. However the stated goal of the guard is defence-in-depth path-traversal rejection and it fails for `..`.
findings.mitigation: Anchor each name segment to require a leading alphanumeric character and ban `..` as a sole segment: change to `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`. This also eliminates the leading-dot case. Alternatively add an explicit `..` rejection clause analogous to the branch `*..*` glob check.

findings.claim: `--i-understand-this-bypasses-the-gate` is silently accepted and silently ignored by the argument parser when provided without `--no-enforce-admins`. The parser sets ACK_ADMIN_BYPASS=1 (line 157) but the gate check (lines 174-188) is inside `if [ "$ENFORCE_ADMINS" != "true" ]` which is not entered when ENFORCE_ADMINS remains "true". No warning is emitted to inform the operator that the acknowledgement flag had no effect.
findings.evidence: enable-required-check.sh line 157: `--i-understand-this-bypasses-the-gate) ACK_ADMIN_BYPASS=1; shift ;;`. Lines 174-188: the outer condition is `if [ "$ENFORCE_ADMINS" != "true" ]` — only entered when --no-enforce-admins was also given. Absent --no-enforce-admins the ACK_ADMIN_BYPASS=1 assignment is a dead assignment; the flag is accepted without any output.
findings.impact: An operator who included `--i-understand-this-bypasses-the-gate` in their invocation without also passing `--no-enforce-admins` (possible if copying a partial invocation template) receives no feedback that the flag was a no-op. Benign in outcome (enforce_admins=true is correct), but could mislead an operator into believing they successfully suppressed the enforce_admins gate when they did not. Silent acceptance with no effect is marginally acceptable but sub-optimal for a safety-critical confirmation flag.
findings.mitigation: After argument parsing, if ACK_ADMIN_BYPASS==1 AND ENFORCE_ADMINS=="true", emit a stderr note: `echo "note: --i-understand-this-bypasses-the-gate has no effect without --no-enforce-admins" >&2`. This removes operator ambiguity at zero safety cost.

findings.claim: `configure-020d2-required-check.sh` (the companion SCP-self script) still carries `"required_signatures": true` in the unified PUT body at line 104, which is the exact pattern CORR-003 was raised and closed for in enable-required-check.sh. The fix-round-1 corrected the adopter script but did not align the companion. The field is silently ignored by GitHub's unified PUT endpoint; `required_signatures` is a dedicated sub-resource. On a fresh SCP-self repo where 020J has not previously run, the 020D2 verification block (line 141-143: `sigs_enabled != "true" → fail=1 → exit 1`) would fail because the PUT never enabled it.
findings.evidence: configure-020d2-required-check.sh line 104: `"required_signatures": true` in the heredoc PUT body. Lines 120-122: `sigs_enabled=$(... .required_signatures.enabled // false)`. Lines 141-143: fail if `sigs_enabled != "true"`. fix-round-1 FIX-ROUND-1.md lists `scripts/enable-required-check.sh` as the only modified script; `configure-020d2-required-check.sh` is not listed. The comment at 020D2:78-80 states "we re-assert it here" implying the author believes the PUT field works, which CORR-003 established it does not. The masking condition noted in R1 CORR-003 evidence (020J ran before 020D2 on SCP-self) explains why this has not been observed in practice yet.
findings.impact: If 020D2 is run against a fresh clone of SCP-self that has not had 020J applied first, it will successfully PUT branch protection then immediately exit 1 on verification. The branch protection shape (minus required_signatures) is in place but the script reports failure, leaving the operator uncertain about state. This is a latent reliability gap not a security regression; real-world impact is suppressed by the 020J prerequisite documented in the script's execution context.
findings.mitigation: Apply the same CORR-003 fix to configure-020d2-required-check.sh: (1) remove `"required_signatures": true` from the PUT heredoc body; (2) add `gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/branches/${DEFAULT_BRANCH}/protection/required_signatures" >/dev/null` after the PUT call; (3) update the inline comment to reflect that required_signatures is managed via the dedicated sub-resource. This aligns both scripts and removes the latent single-operator failure mode.

structured_review.summary: All three R1 MAJ findings (CORR-001 fence nesting, CORR-002 SCRIPT_SHA empty fallback, CORR-003 required_signatures in unified PUT) are confirmed closed. R1 MIN findings CORR-004 (jq null-guard) and CORR-005 (before-state error discrimination) are confirmed closed. R1 nits CORR-006 (shift-2 guards) and CORR-007 (python3 require_cmd) are confirmed closed. Checklist items 1-9, 11, 13-14 pass cleanly. Three new findings: CORR2-001 (MIN) is a regression from fix-round-1 — the SAF-010 fall-through implementation left 'verification passed ✓' unconditionally emitting on failure, producing contradictory attended output and a false-positive in any captured log; CORR2-002 (MIN) is a defence-in-depth gap in the repo path-traversal regex which accepts owner/.. despite that being a traversal primitive; CORR2-004 (MIN) is the CORR-003 fix not being applied to the companion configure-020d2-required-check.sh, leaving a latent verification failure for 020D2 on repos without prior 020J execution. One nit (CORR2-003): silent ignore of --i-understand-this-bypasses-the-gate without --no-enforce-admins gives no operator feedback. No CRIT or MAJ findings. Verdict CONDITIONAL: the script is functionally correct for happy-path adopter onboarding but CORR2-001 should be fixed before merge (misleading output on failure is a correctness regression) and CORR2-002 and CORR2-004 should be addressed in the same pass.
